question: An ASHA worker asks your advice at a community camp. An apparently healthy breastfed infant is now 5 months and 3 weeks old. The grandmother is insisting the baby should start rice gruel and dal water because 'summer is coming and breast milk alone is not enough.' What is the most appropriate counselling message?

answers.text: Agree with the grandmother — supplemental water and thin liquids are safe during hot weather and do not count as complementary foods

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is incorrect and dangerous. Exclusive breastfeeding means NO water, liquids, or other foods regardless of season or temperature. Breast milk is sufficient hydration even in hot climates — this is a common misconception (the 'water trap').

answers.text: Start thin rice gruel immediately since the infant is near 6 months and delay may cause nutritional deficiency

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: At 5 months 3 weeks, the infant has not yet completed 6 months (26 completed weeks). Starting solids before 6 months increases the risk of infections, allergy, and displaces breast milk. Wait until the 6-month mark.

answers.text: Continue exclusive breastfeeding until 6 completed months; complementary foods should start at exactly 6 months alongside continued breastfeeding

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The WHO/IAP recommendation is exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 completed months (26 weeks), with no other foods or liquids including water. Complementary foods begin at 6 months, with breastfeeding continuing for 2 years or beyond.

answers.text: Begin semi-solid foods at 5 months since the infant shows feeding readiness cues such as watching adults eat

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Feeding readiness cues (watching adults eat, loss of tongue-extrusion reflex) are supporting evidence but the WHO/IAP guideline is explicit: exclusive breastfeeding for 6 completed months. Individual readiness signs do not override the 6-month recommendation.

overallFeedback.feedback: WHO/IAP guidelines are unambiguous: exclusive breastfeeding for 6 completed months (no water, no liquids, no foods). Complementary feeding starts at exactly 6 months alongside continued breastfeeding.
Correct. Exclusive breastfeeding continues for exactly 6 completed months with absolutely no other food or liquid. Complementary foods begin at 6 months with continued breastfeeding to 2 years.
